summary: Jeskola Bass's line plays on Neo Poly as a mono legato bass: notes as notes (in its pitch convention), slides as glides, volume as velocity; cutoff, resonance and waveform carry over.

rules.why: measured (Windows, NativeSuccessorCalibration): the brightness (spectral centroid) of a held A2 at Jeskola Bass's cutoff 10, 32, 64, 96 and 128 is Neo Poly's saw through its Ladder 24 at 1.7, 5.3, 10.5, 14.7 and 16 kHz (at 0 Jeskola Bass is silent)

notes.why: Each row's note lasts to the track's next; Slide note glides to it over Slide lenght ticks; Volume (0x80 = 100 %, it holds) is the velocity, 0x80 → 64, with Vel → amp at 100 % and Volume +6 dB making up for it.

remarks: No new machine (machine-safety.md §4, H4): Neo Poly in Legato with glide plays the bass line; its ladder filter and envelopes take the cutoff, resonance and envelope settings.

The cutoff and envelope scales are assumed (closed source: the texts are bare 0–100 % or 0–128): a cutoff of 0 % is laid on 80 Hz and 100 % on 16 kHz, logarithmically; the timbres differ, the notes, their lengths, slides and loudness carry over.
Jeskola Bass has no filter envelope: Neo Poly's F1 env is set to 0 %.

tolerance.measured: Windows, a bass line (8 notes) before and after: its default saw +0.5 dB; notes in tune. Elak_SVF.bmx's Jeskola Bass (its cutoff low) −1.3 dB with the measured cutoff (−11.2 dB with the cutoff assumed before)
tolerance.why_not: Not measured per band: the filters and oscillators are different models, so the timbre differs (the cutoff is matched by brightness, the spectral centroid); loudness is matched (the output gain) and checked.

evidence: Machines/Manifests/Generators/Jeskola Bass.machine.json (draft: descriptions give 0–0x80 scales, Waveform 1–3, Volume 0x80 = 100 %, slide length in ticks)
